# Research: Hierarchical LLM-Efficient Security Scanning

Phase 0 output. All Technical Context unknowns resolved below. Two external research tracks (R1, R2) were executed; R3–R6 were resolved from domain standards and the clarified spec decisions.

## R1 — Per-agent installation: skill/command conventions

**Decision**: Ship an **agent-agnostic core skill** in the Agent Skills open format (`<name>/SKILL.md` + `scripts/` + `schemas/` + `prompts/`), generated by a Spec Kit-style installer into per-agent locations via thin adapters. v1 adapter targets: Claude Code (`.claude/skills/`), GitHub Copilot (`.github/skills/`), Cursor (`.cursor/skills/`), Windsurf (`.windsurf/skills/`), Devin (`.devin/skills/`), plus the cross-vendor `.agents/skills/` path. Gemini CLI gets a translated `.gemini/commands/*.toml` adapter. Aider is out of scope (no custom-command mechanism).

**Rationale**: `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description` required) is the de-facto common denominator — Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf, and Devin all load it and support multi-file skill directories. Spec Kit's `specify init --ai <agent>` proves the adapter model at scale; its registrar pattern (dir, format, extension, argument placeholder per agent) is directly reusable.

**Alternatives considered**: single universal file with no adapters (breaks Gemini TOML and per-agent frontmatter needs); manual clone-and-copy (rejected in spec Q1 — installer command chosen); targeting one reference agent only (rejected in spec Q2).

**Adapter transformation rules** (from research):
- Core `SKILL.md` uses only safe frontmatter (`name`, `description`, `license`, `metadata`); agent-specific fields (`triggers`, `disable-model-invocation`, `argument-hint`) are added by adapters.
- Gemini adapter converts YAML frontmatter + Markdown body → TOML (`prompt = """..."""`, `description`), and `$ARGUMENTS` → `{{args}}`.
- Installer validates `name` matches directory and `description` non-empty before writing.

Refs: agentskills.io/specification; code.claude.com/docs/en/skills; docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/add-skills; cursor.com/docs/skills; docs.devin.ai/cli/extensibility/skills/creating-skills; google-gemini.github.io/gemini-cli/docs/cli/custom-commands.html; github.github.io/spec-kit/reference/integrations.html.

## R2 — Multi-language code graph extraction

**Decision**: Build the extractor on **py-tree-sitter v0.26+ with per-language grammar wheels** (`tree-sitter-python`, `tree-sitter-java`, `tree-sitter-javascript`, `tree-sitter-typescript`, `tree-sitter-go`), a per-language `Query`-based extraction layer emitting normalized per-file facts, and a deterministic merge into the JSON code graph (sorted collections, stable IDs `<repo>:<path>#<symbol>`). Heuristic enrichers detect HTTP entry points (Flask/FastAPI/Django/Express/Spring/Gin), DB access (ORM calls, raw SQL), and framework metadata via decorator/annotation patterns. Language-specific parsers (`ast`, `ljavalang`, `esprima`, `go/ast`) serve as fallbacks when a grammar fails.

**Rationale**: one parser interface across all v1 languages; deterministic and error-tolerant on broken files; prebuilt wheels; fast enough (~1M LOC parses in seconds-to-tens-of-seconds with multiprocessing; cold-run target < 30 s). The accepted v1 limitation: call edges are best-effort/name-based — precise call-target resolution (SCIP/Joern/LSP) is deferred to a later deep-analysis tier since those tools require working build environments, defeating the "deterministic, fast, dependency-light" requirement.

**Alternatives considered**: Joern/CPG (heavyweight JVM, not JSON-first — deferred to v2 taint analysis); SCIP/LSIF indexers (need build environments — deferred to v2); Semgrep `AST_generic` (LGPL + unstable internal CLI surface — borrow query patterns only); language servers (nondeterministic timing, per-language setup); `code2graph-rs` (pre-0.1 beta — watch, don't bet); `stakgraph`/`graphmy` (full apps, not libraries).

**Determinism checklist** (from research): pin grammar versions; parse from bytes (UTF-8); normalized `/` paths; sort all node/edge arrays before serialization; multiprocessing (not threads) for CPU-bound extraction.

Refs: github.com/tree-sitter/py-tree-sitter; github.com/joernio/joern; github.com/scip-code/scip; github.com/NodeDB-Lab/code2graph.

## R3 — External scanner adapters (reference tools per category)

**Decision**: One reference adapter per category (spec Q5): **Semgrep** (SAST, JSON output), **Gitleaks** (secrets, JSON), **OSV-Scanner** (dependencies, JSON), **Trivy** (IaC, JSON — config scanning mode). Adapters parse each tool's JSON into the normalized Finding schema; tools are invoked only when present on the system (init's environment check reports them), and ingested findings retain original rule IDs alongside normalized CWE mappings (FR-012).

**Rationale**: all four are open-source, JSON-emitting, widely adopted, and cover the four mandated categories; adapter-per-tool keeps the pipeline tool-agnostic.

**Alternatives considered**: SARIF as the single universal ingestion format (good future addition — adapters already normalize to one schema, so a SARIF adapter later subsumes many tools); CodeQL (heavy setup, database build step — poor fit for zero-config v1).

## R4 — LLM provider batch APIs (external-endpoint mode)

**Decision**: Behind a provider abstraction with two operations: `submit_batch(items) → job_handle` and `poll(job_handle) → results | pending | failed`. v1 supports Anthropic Message Batches and OpenAI Batch API semantics (both: async job, ~50% cost discount, results within hours). Expired/failed items fall back to interactive calls and are recorded (FR-016b).

**Rationale**: both major providers expose materially identical batch semantics, so a thin abstraction avoids provider lock-in; off-peak scheduling is implemented as "submit batch when window opens" plus local queueing in the scan state.

**Alternatives considered**: per-provider bespoke integrations (rejected — adapter pattern already proven for scanners/agents); local queue-only "batching" without provider APIs (no cost discount — the point of the feature).

## R5 — Secret redaction engine (FR-006a)

**Decision**: Deterministic redaction stage before any model call, layered: (1) Gitleaks-style rule packs for known credential formats (API keys, tokens, private-key blocks, connection strings), (2) entropy detection for unknown high-entropy strings, (3) config-defined custom patterns. Unsure content is blocked + warned (spec edge case), never passed through. Redaction metadata (`blocked_items` count) is recorded per context packet.

**Rationale**: deterministic, auditable, and testable with fixture secrets; no ML component (keeps determinism guarantees); layered rules catch both known formats and novel secrets.

**Alternatives considered**: LLM-based redaction (non-deterministic, self-defeating — sends secrets to a model to decide what not to send); regex-only single layer (misses high-entropy unknowns).

## R6 — CWE/OWASP mapping data

**Decision**: Ship a curated JSON mapping (CWE ID → OWASP Top 10 category → well-established compliance control refs where unambiguous) as versioned data inside the skill payload. Primary source: MITRE CWE list; OWASP's official CWE↔Top 10 mapping. Only mappings with direct, unambiguous relationships are included (spec Q3 refinement).

**Rationale**: static, versioned data keeps mapping deterministic and offline-capable; opportunistic compliance refs avoid interpretation liability.

**Alternatives considered**: live lookup from MITRE APIs (network dependency, nondeterministic); LLM-assigned CWE IDs without validation (hallucinated IDs — rejected; IDs must validate against the shipped CWE set).

## Resolved Technical Context summary

| Item | Resolution |
|------|-----------|
| Language/Version | Python 3.11+ |
| Graph extraction | py-tree-sitter + grammar wheels (R2) |
| Agent install | Agent Skills `SKILL.md` core + per-agent adapters (R1) |
| Scanner adapters | Semgrep / Gitleaks / OSV-Scanner / Trivy (R3) |
| Batch APIs | Provider abstraction over Anthropic/OpenAI batch semantics (R4) |
| Redaction | Deterministic layered rules + entropy (R5) |
| Standards data | Versioned CWE→OWASP→compliance JSON (R6) |
